html:
German East Africa was a colony of Germany from 1885 to 1919, covering what are now mainland Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi. The map shows it in 1914.

It began with treaties signed in 1884 by the adventurer Carl Peters, whose company Germany backed. Resistance was fierce. The coast rose in 1888, and the Hehe under Mkwawa beat a German column in 1891 and held out for years. The Maji Maji rebellion of 1905 to 1907, against forced cotton growing, was crushed by famine and war; perhaps a hundred thousand or more people died.

The Germans built railways from the coast to Lake Tanganyika and Lake Victoria. In World War I the commander Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck led a guerrilla campaign that lasted until after the armistice in Europe, at a terrible cost to African porters and villagers. After the war Britain took most of the colony as Tanganyika, and Belgium took Ruanda-Urundi.
sum: German East Africa was a colony of Germany from 1885 to 1919, covering what are now mainland Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi. The map shows it in 1914.
